reviews.comment: Class seems easy at first, but ramps up after first exam. This professor lectured quickly and used terms without fully explaining them, which made him difficult to follow. However, you can tell he knows the course content and answered questions well. Also provides lots of practice problems before exams. Homework and quizzes are fairly easy.

Homrighausen is a good professor, who grades very fairly and gives you a ton of resources to succeed. My main gripe is that his lectures are just largely uninspired and are reading of a series of preset slides.

There's a lot of flexibility in this class, but make sure you understand the material. The final exam replaces your worst midterm. Really good teacher, but could be better if he had coded during the classes more as well.

He's a decent professor but has a very generous grading policy (35% of your grade is free). He posts tons of practice problems for the exams. If you focus on learning how to use R studio, it is very easy to get an A in this class.

Deceptively difficult class. Dr. H is a good lecturer and is pretty funny, and he posts all his lectures online for those who need them. Weekly HW and Quizzes are pretty easy and the final replaces the lowest midterm grade.

The professor seems like a decent guy and knows his stuff. He taught from slides, which seemed disorganized to me and didn't really fit my learning style, but might fit other peoples'. Every week there is a quiz for a completion grade and online homework. Exams seem harder than the homework. I'd try another prof, but you'll be fine if you have him.

Not much to say as class is very cut and dry. Weekly quizzes that you can retake as many times as necessary, and bi-weekly homework assignments are what you are graded on. I have a coding background, so it was easier for me to understand different syntax and methods, but he explains things very well. No exams. Would take him again, no problem.
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Clear lectures which could be a little boring at times. Big focus on R and provided samples that could be used during the test, which made calculating a lot easier. Exams were definitely tougher than homework and the reviews he gives beforehand aren't always helpful. Overall solid professor for a class that is more difficult than advertised.
Lectures are sometimes interactive and/or funny. Homework is pretty easy. Exams have parts, but don't have partial credit. Be comfortable using R.

3 Exams total, but replaces the smallest midterm with the grade from the final, which saved my A. All his homework and his quizzes were basically free points. I found it impossible to stay awake in class and eventually stopped attending. Great teacher but not for everyone. The phrase "may be too smart to teach Stat 211" is definitely true.

Exams are very difficult and exam reviews are nothing like the exams. He is a good person but not a good professor. He goes over the material but doesn't explain it very well. His lectures are recorded so attendance is not mandatory. Only one homework assignment per week and they're pretty easy. If you can, try getting a different professor.

Decent, did his job and tried to make lectures interesting. Charismatic guy but people stop showing up to class since he records all his lectures. I will say he often throws around a lot of vocab when he's teaching that we don't fully understand yet, so if you haven't taken a stats course before this could be challenging. Exams aren't too bad.

Real chill guy.
Yes, there is hw every week, but it's not that difficult considering that you're given 5 tries for each question. 
The lecture are recorded which is apparent after the 2nd week when the class size decreases to a fourth.
And the exams are really similar to the homeworks, so make sure that you know how to do each question.
reviews.ratingTags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Clear lectures

Lectures can be hard to understand, sometimes phrased confusingly/more wordy. Good professor, he knows a lot of info and is good with R. Exams are difficult imo despite having taken AP Stats. Pay attention, go to the lecture (or watch recorded lectures), and ask questions, otherwise, it makes it much harder to get a good grade!
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: IMO Homrighausen is a critically underrated professor. Yes, his class is hard, but such is STAT 211. He is kind, approachable, records his lectures, and makes an effort to make them interesting and applicable. What's not to love? His tests, admittedly, are timed too shortly, but it's not anything absolutely egregious. I'm a big fan, personally.

As a stats major, this class came fairly easy to me. This is not the case for everyone though. Attendance is not mandatory, and it is very noticeable 2 weeks into class. I would say to just watch the lectures he uploads tbh. His tests are EXTREMELY difficult. Although they are open note, there is just no possible way to finish in time. HW is easy.

You will learn a LOT of ML concepts here that you can get asked in interviews, so it's great material. The assignments are not difficult with how many code examples he gives and he doesn't have exams, only HW and a semester-long group project. This a great class to brush up on things from the beginning to the end of a DS/ML project, but all in R

He gave pretty condescending responses when people asked questions and refused to help with general questions. He also gave exam reviews that were nothing like the exams, for the exams it is better to practice the homework problems. His teaching style was mostly theory based, so it was difficult to do the homework & exam based only off the lecture
Great professor, teaches well and is easily approachable. Would definitely recommend for STAT 211.

Decent lectures with not too much homework. Be wary for exams, as they can be quite difficult especially in the amount of time allotted even though they are open note. Definitely attend the review session and be comfortable with homework problems before an exam.

Very knowledgeable professor, he is an expert in R and Python. It is easier to come in with a Python background, but his homeworks are very similar to his lectures and you can use his code from there. Python is mostly covered, with R at the end. He goes deep into programming concepts. You will learn a lot in his class, highly recommend! W professor

(Coming from a Stat major). His teaching style is hard to grasp but asking questions helps clarify. I recommend learning how the concepts connect outside of class. He's very helpful during office hours. Quizzes and homework are easy. Tests/Final are all online over Zoom. You're allowed to use notes, Google, R Code to help you on exams.

Very knowledgeable but hard to understand. I think he is too smart to be teaching 211. Tests are open note but sooo much material, I ran out of time. Final can replace lowest exam, and easy quizzes that arent worth much. Make sure to ask proper questions in class or he will correct you and tell you your question isnt an actual question.

Exams are very heavy, there's only 2. Weekly quizzes and HW balance that, and final can replace low exam. Lectures are recorded + posted online, it's still best to attend as quiz passwords are said in class. Spends too much time on theory, not enough on examples/problem solving skills. Exams are HARD, and "require" RStudio coding for calculations.
reviews.ratingTags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He says "No prerequisites will be assumed," but if you don't have any calculus background, then you will find this class to be more difficult. This is basically a computer science Python coding class with calculus thrown in on the homework. R is not taught much. I wish I had known all this before taking the class -- I wouldn't have taken it then.

Professor clearly understands the material he teaches very well. Somewhat of a boring core (but important) class, but he does a good job of still making content engaging. Attendance quizzes, WebAssign homeworks. Tests are open note and very reasonable.
Dr. Homrighausen is very knowledgeable and an excellent teacher! I am glad I got to take STAT 636 with him.

Pretty cool guy, and clearly very smart. Sadly, this means he uses very hard-to-understand language at times. Lectures are good and use real-world examples. Hw is a pain and takes long. Tests are hard, even with open notes, bc of the sheer amt of material. Do not mistake it as a math class, it's an applied math class, you'll learn it's not the same

Despite STAT 211 being an intro class, expect to work very hard if you're taking it with Prof Homrighausen. Homework assignments are difficult and time consuming. Exams, although open note, are just as difficult, so you will still need to study for them like you would for a closed note exam.

I may have gotten an A, but it is only because he heavily curved tests. The first couple lectures are easy and then he assumes you understand and doesn't take kindly to questions. Office hours are extremely helpful. But yeah HW takes several hours bc it is challenging. I just wish he would go slower and explain more. This possible but difficult.
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The first few lectures were great but later on the professor really rushes through the material. His language can be very sophisticated at times which can be a hurdle while trying to grasp new information. However, he is knowledgeable about statistics, which is why he would be great for higher level classes, but not intro classes.
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The course is organized into two parts: keystone topics and special topics. The special topics, based on students' interests, are added later in the semester and motivated some interesting discussions. I think this organization provides 2 benefits, 1) it motivates students to explore topics, 2) the discussion is inspiring.
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Homrighausen seemed pretty friendly and clearly explained things the first few lectures but after a while he just started rushing through material and assuming we knew how to work everything. Anytime someone would ask him a question he would act as if it was stupid that we didn't know already.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This is the application side of 636, and Dr H ensures that you pick up some new tools to make the most of data cleaning, model selection, parameter and hyperparameter optimization, etc. If you're interested in data science, a sequence of 636 and 656 with Dr H is a no-brainer

Dr H ensures that you really know the fundamentals - you won't survive on rote memorization, and that's for the better. His lectures are thorough, clear, and meaningful. 50% of the grade comes from HW with fair deadlines. Get down to the meaning behind the lectures and you'll do well on the closed-notes exams

Bad lecturer. Terrible handwriting. Honestly if you can, take this course from a different professor. Hes fairly new and makes an easy class unnecessarily difficult. He did provide some extra credit and curved the exams, but only because the class averages were terrible. Had material been taught in a better manner, this wouldnt have happened.

Dr. H is a tough one. He makes a class that is supposed to be easy... quite tough. His handwriting is illegible so good luck with lecture notes. I managed to get an A through outside tutoring and very little extra credit. He did curve the exams, but only because the class averages were trash. I had to work extremely hard for this non-major class
reviews.ratingTags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: His lectures are extremely confusing. I did not understand what was going in the lectures half the time as it's usually just him deriving some complicated stats formula. His tests are EZ if you have taken AP stats though. And if you do the HW, the tests are pretty easy too. His reviews never explain the answers, so theyre not the greatest.
reviews.ratingTags: Accessible outside class--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Very nice professor and really cares for his students. His lectures can sometimes be boring because of his voice and heavy use of jargon. He is always available to help and is really understanding. He does go off topic sometimes and his examples can be overly complex compared to the material being covered.

Knows statistics very well, but his class is difficult. Tests are hard and math-heavy. Most people did bad on them but he gave us some good opportunities to raise our grade. Not an easy A at all: do the HW, go to the (optional) labs, and ask him questions. Ended up dropping b/c I fell behind due to family stuff and it was too much to catch back up
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Don't trust the other reviews, if you pay attention, ask questions and most importantly do the homework legit it is a very doable class, if you ask him to reexplain some of the jargon he tends to use the class will be even clearer. He tries to make sure you not only know how to do the material but understand it!

I scored below average on the first test, but he's given us a few opportunities to raise our grade so I'll probably end up with an A. I spent countless hours on the 2nd midterm review trying to understand the material and came out with an A without studying with any other material, so those reviewers aren't being honest with you or themselves..

It's true that the reviews are very involved and don't help as much as you'd like/assume. Doing the reviews helps you get 40ish points on the exams, which is clearly beneficial (So worth understanding), but not a game-changer. In all honesty, his lectures are bad. The required textbook is poorly written. You're given few study materials for tests.

Dr. Homrighausen is a nice guy, but he's not a great professor. He is INCREDIBLY knowledgeable in statistics, but he's not quite as capable at teaching an intro level class. Make sure you know the math behind the concepts. His lectures are conceptually based, but his tests are math HEAVY, and the reviews don't help much.
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Darren is a very nice guy, but he teaches the class as if everyone is an expert on the subject already. I found it difficult to keep up in class even after reading the material in the book thoroughly. Also, there is not much help for the tests. His "test reviews" do not even explain the answers and is not very relevant to the test.

He's smart, definitely knows his stuff but can't get it across to his students easily. He'll explain things down to deriving it and that's great and all but for an introductory statistics course, that's a bit much. There's no doubt he's an expert in what he does but he doesn't make the lectures simple enough for students to understand. Beware.

Dr. Homrighausen is undoubtedly THE WORST PROFESSOR I've ever had. What's the point of a 40 question test review if the test will be nothing like it? Like this first test we took, this one will probably also get curved HEAVILY. He'll blame our low grades on us again and indirectly call us morons. This is going to be the first non-A grade. Avoid him

Dr. H shows his inexperience. He's not very assertive around the classroom, and although he tries earnestly to engage the students, often he'll ask a question and noone will respond for a full minute. However, he is extremely caring and earnest. If you come to him with any questions, he will be glad to help you. Do your homework, tests are great.

Knows his stuff. Very responsive. Young and in touch with the latest, coolest statistical techniques. Tests were closed notes and conceptual. He is good at making sure youre tested on understanding and not on parroting back what youve heard. For example, class examples for a certain concept were in 2D but the related test question was in 1D.
